entries.title: Zechariah 8:2
segments:
vv 2-3. 
 
Though God will chastise his people for their sins, he will not suffer their enemies to triumph over them perpetually; but will save them for the glory of his own name, and that he may fulfil to them his gracious promises.

entries.title: Zechariah 8:4
segments:
vv 4-5. 
 
God's blessing fills a community with health, peace, and joy, and brings its citizens to a vigorous and cheerful old age; but these temporal effects are only a symbol of that nobler spiritual life, strength, and joy which his gospel brings to he souls of all who receive it.

entries.title: Zechariah 8:6
segments:
Marvellous; a thing that seems too wonderful to be expected. 
 
Nothing is too hard for the Lord.  With infinite ease he brings to pass the most surprising changes in the condition of his afflicted people.

entries.title: Zechariah 8:10
segments: No hire for man--hire for beasts; no profit from the labor of man or beast.

entries.title: Zechariah 8:16
segments:
Judgment of truth and peace; judgment in accordance with truth, the effect of which is to establish peace. 
 
vv 16-17. 
 
God's promises are connected with the obedience of his people, and cannot be fulfilled except they hearken to his voice, and walk in the ways of his appointment.

entries.title: Zechariah 8:19
segments: The fourth month; when Jerusalem was taken.
Tenth; the month when the siege of Jerusalem began.
Shall be--joy and gladness; shall be turned into joy and gladness. After rebuking the people for their sins, Jehovah returns a gracious answer to their inquiry.
It is God's way, first to rebuke his people for their sins, that he may humble them; and then grant them a gracious answer to their requests.

entries.title: Zechariah 8:20
segments: People; in the original, peoples, that is, nations; for this is a prophecy of the conversion of the nations to Jehovah in the latter days.  It was fulfilled only in a limited manner while the second temple was standing.  Its highest fulfilment is under the Christian dispensation.

vv 20-23. 
 
When God forsakes his people because of their sins, they are weak and despised by the world; but the moment they return to him, his blessing makes them strong and prosperous; and then multitudes of those without, seeing that God is with them, join themselves to their number.

entries.title: Zechariah 8:23
segments: Him that is a Jew; instead of being despised and persecuted, the Jew shall now be honored by all nations, and they shall seek his God as their God.  The true heirs of this promise are the children of Abraham by faith in Christ, who are Jews, not outwardly, but inwardly, in the spirit, and not in the letter.
